message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported, for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, revenue of $1.85 billion, net income of $397 million, a gross margin of 65.87 per cent, a net margin of 21.51 per cent and earnings per share of 2.82 [D1]. Revenue rose 36.54 per cent and net income rose 107.85 per cent from a year earlier, and earnings per share beat the 2.16 estimate by 30.56 per cent [D1]. The fourth fiscal quarter is guided to revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion, roughly 37 per cent growth at the mid-point, and to earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 on 172 million diluted shares [D1].

The market's first verdict was negative, with the shares falling 6.32 per cent in the session on 2026-08-19 after the 2026-08-18 release, and the argument is now about which force dominates [D1]. The bull reading is that demand is the story, with management saying wireline orders more than doubled and that demand is far exceeding the ability to supply [D3]. The bear reading uses the same call, where management said the supply environment is less flexible than a year earlier and that supply chain would remain the governor of near-term revenue for the next several quarters [D3]. The bear side also notes that revenue rose 7.51 per cent on the quarter before, and that one-time tariff impacts artificially pulled up fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat [D1] [D3].

The plan is therefore to judge the next report against the guided range of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion in revenue and 3.34 to 3.40 in earnings per share, and to treat revenue at or below the low end as confirmation that supply, not demand, is capping conversion [D1]. The operating reference points to hold are Communications Solutions Group revenue of $1,345 million and Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue of $501 million, since the growth in the latest quarter ran through both segments [D1]. Because management frames the limit as supply rather than demand, commentary on deconstraining the supply chain carries as much weight as the headline figures [D3]. The plan also assumes the current margin is a high bar rather than a base, given the non-repeating tariff benefit [D4].

The next checkpoints are management's scheduled investor conference appearances, which offer an earlier read on the supply language than the following results release [D6]. Until that language changes from constrained to improving, the useful signal is the conversion of demand into revenue rather than the level of demand itself [D3].
